turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I'm Meredith Kalinowski, Owen's mother, and I have until 4:40. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
"We found." Who is we, Hale, and what exactly did you find? I'm writing this down, so start with the zero: when was it entered, and why did Owen learn about it from the gradebook on his phone?
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.
A creation time isn't a decision, Hale. Procedure 4.2 says you call me before any mark is entered, and nobody called. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
Did you speak to Owen under 4.1 before you entered a zero, and why did nobody call me under 4.2?
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
Don't manage me, Hale. You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in.
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.
I'm writing that down. A student misquoting a line from memory is an error in an essay, Hale, not a finding. Show me the line in his essay.
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Save it, Hale. I asked to see the line in his essay, and I'm still waiting.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.
I'm writing that down. Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale, that's what revising is. Do you have the outline here, with its date on it?
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.

That's a machine's guess, Hale. Turnitin's own guide says its indicator should not be used as the sole basis for adverse action against a student, and procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern. You still haven't put that outline in front of me.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
Off the record doesn't exist in this room, Hale. Are you asking me to do your job? Withdraw the zero, and then show me the outline.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.

That's 4.4, and I want it in writing, with nothing in his record and nothing in front of his class. But a rewrite for what, Hale? You haven't put a single document in front of me, and I'm not taking a deal that admits something.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? I have a call at 4:40. Where is the outline?
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.
Go ahead, Hale. I'm going to the principal's office when we're done here, and I want that threat in an email. The zero comes off, and you still haven't shown me one document.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Neither. The zero comes off. Ten minutes.
